well: IODP Hole 354-U1452C - LOWER BENGAL FAN, Bay of Bengal (8.0068 N, 87.1819 E; seafloor -3,671.5 m), on the 8-degree-N transect across the LARGEST SEDIMENT BODY ON EARTH - the submarine fan that archives the erosion of the Himalaya; IODP Expedition 354 (2015), record spans 0.01-4.69 m CSF-A carrying ~193.5 kyr of monsoonal history
operator_on_log: Weber, Lantzsch, Dekens, Das, Reilly, Martos, Meyer-Jacob, Agrahari, Ekblad, Titschack, Holmes & Wolfgramm (Bonn/Bremen et al.) - Beckman Coulter LS 13320 laser-diffraction granulometry on the terrigenous fraction (organic carbon, biogenic carbonate and opal chemically removed per the file's own comment); dual GEOCODES: depth AND age model

coverage: COMPLETE DATASET: 235 mean-grain-size measurements on a perfectly uniform 2-cm grid, 0.01-4.69 m, with the published age model riding as a second geocode (0.533-193.538 ka BP) - hemipelagic monsoonal background ~3-8 units punctuated by coarse event beds, the largest a 7-sample turbidite at 1.75-1.87 m peaking at 53.9
curves: Depth sed [m] 0.01-4.69 (GEOCODE; all 234 steps exactly 0.02 m)
Age [ka BP] 0.533-193.538 (second GEOCODE, loads as a channel; strictly increasing)
Grain size mean ['phi' per the header - see anomaly disclosure] 2.966-53.900
source_anomaly_disclosure: ONE source quirk preserved verbatim and proven by physics: the grain-size unit is labeled [phi] but the VALUES cannot be phi - the maximum, 53.9, would mean 2^-53.9 mm = 6e-17 mm, five orders below an atomic nucleus, and even the background 3-8 range behaves as MICRONS (3-8 um = fine silt/clay, exactly the hemipelagic monsoon lithology of the source paper) - the archive carries micron values under a phi unit label, detected by impossibility, carried unchanged; noted also: one isolated coarse sample near the core top (29.11 at 0.07 m) alongside the contiguous event bed
purpose: forty-first catalogue entry - the BENGAL FAN / BAY OF BENGAL joins as region TWENTY-NINE (the largest sediment body on Earth: the Himalaya's erosion archive) and laser granulometry is kind THIRTY; the physics headline is a two-witness turbidite: the SEVEN contiguous coarse samples at 1.75-1.87 m (15.57-53.90, the only contiguous run above 15) coincide EXACTLY with the age model's plateau - per-step age increments of 0.0013-0.0014 ka against a background median of 0.8604 ka, a 615x time compression meaning ~14 cm deposited in about a DECADE - the event bed announced independently by grain size and by time standing still, the same event-deposit physics the catalogue carries from the Dead Sea (one scanned debrite) and El'gygytgyn (the full inventory), now witnessed by an age model
verified: 235 rows / 235 counted cells against the header's own Size declaration (EXACT - both geocodes excluded by the PANGAEA counting convention); uniform 0.02-m grid on all 234 increments; age strictly increasing across all 234 steps; exactly 8 samples above 15 (1 isolated near-surface + 7 contiguous at 1.75-1.87 m, maximum 53.90 at 1.85 m); event-bed age steps 0.0013-0.0014 ka vs background median 0.8604 ka (615x compression); the phi-impossibility quantified (2^-53.9 mm = 5.95e-17 mm); gate-pinned; source URL serves the identical dataset
